transcript: Spoilers for wicked for good. But I just got back from seeing it again and I have to talk about one of my favourite changes made for the stage, which is adding Glinda to wonderful. Really, it's both adding Glinda to wonderful and also the fact that Elphaba goes to Glinda before going to the Wizard. This not only strengthens their relationship through throughout the entire story, but it also strengthens Fiyero as a character. I also think it strengthens the overall story of what wicked is trying to say. And it really starts off with that scene where Elphaba goes directly to Glinda. And literally the first thing that Glinda does when she realises that Elphaba is there is, go, please come inside before the monkeys see you. Worrying about elphaba’s safety in a way that nobody else that she has encountered on her journey has done, with the exception of Dulcibear. Like, even though all this time has passed, we really get to see that these two still mean so much to each other before the Fiyero of it all comes into play, which I think makes the ultimate payoff of for good make that much more sense. And then we get this beautiful contrast between Glinda and Fiyero, because Glinda's first reaction to wanting to protect the Elphaba is to bring her into this system, because that's the system that she is comfortable in, even though it is a system that has been directly attacking Elphaba. Compare that to Fiyero’s first instinct to protect Elphaba is to directly attack the system that has been attacking her, sacrificing his own comfort in the process. They both are utilizing their positions in this system in vastly different ways. I also think that this chain of events now strengthens Glinda's character because we see Glinda be reunited with her friend, thinking that she is going to help her friend, and then the next time that she sees Elphaba, Elphaba has destroyed her wedding and stolen her man. And because Glinda doesn't have the context for what Elphaba experienced while Glinda was busy heading to the altar, it makes Glinda's actions and Glinda turning on Elphaba that much more justified in Glinda's head, even though we as the audience know the full story. And because we have that Elfie Glinda reunion earlier on and go through all of wonderful, it only strengthens the fact that Fiyero is the first person that she meets in this entire film that is literally just going to join her cause, no questions asked. She doesn't ask him for help. He sacrifices his position to join her. So, like, yeah, I too would put on a cardigan in the woods. Seeing Glinda in this sequence also makes the payoff when Glinda finally is able to sacrifice her own comfort to run after Elphaba make that much more of an impact. And it makes the redemption arc that Glinda gets that much more earned. And As an added bonus, Wonderful's no longer a skip track. This is now a great song. And, uh. And there's so many great moments in the sequence. This is one of the moments I looked forward to the most. There's something so devastating about getting to see these two friends reunite and capture some of the joy that in the stage version is really only there in one short day. And then it never appears again.
